description: Clips the signal at 'gate' and imposes a WAVEFORM of frequency 'freq' onto the clipped stretches (submode 2 - the pitched sibling of overload 1's noise fill). Duration static and SAMPLE-EXACT on all probes; deterministic. Output rescaled like submode 1 (peak ~ gate/(1+gate): 0.2308 at 0.3). depth and freq are both breakpoint-capable (each verified against both scalar endpoints; a near-constant freq brk renders byte-identical to the scalar - the brk path is healthy here, unlike the gate slot). gate has the same broken-breakpoint behavior as submode 1's clip_level - keep it scalar. Works on any material including unipolar. MONO only.
musical_use: Distortion that sings: loud stretches don't just clip, they get replaced by a buzzing tone at freq - effectively an amplitude-keyed oscillator ride-along. Tune freq to the source (octave, fifth) for aggressive but pitched overdrive, or detune/sweep it for siren-like interference. Low gate values replace most of the sound with the imposed waveform (approaching hard sync-buzz); high values only colour the peaks. Breakpoint freq to gliss the buzz through the file - the classic move is a slow rise so the distortion appears to sharpen and lift. Use overload 1 when you want noise-crust instead of pitch.

gate.description: Clipping ceiling, 0-1 (range shared with submode 1, refusal verbatim). SCALAR ONLY: the breakpoint path in this slot collapses output to a fixed near-silent render regardless of values (verified in submode 1, same parameter machinery). 0 renders digital silence.

depth.description: Depth of the waveform pattern on clipped stretches, 0-1. Breakpoint-capable (verified in the shared depth slot: ramp differs from both endpoints).

freq.description: Frequency of the waveform imposed on clipped stretches (CDP-enforced 0.01 Hz to Nyquist: 60000 refused 'out of range (0.010000 to 22050.000000)'; 0.05 accepted - sub-audio 'gating' legal). Breakpoint-capable, banner-confirmed and verified (200->2000 ramp differs from both endpoint renders; near-constant brk == scalar byte-identical).

examples.description: Pitched overdrive tuned an octave above a 440 Hz source.
examples.expected_use: Loud stretches buzz at 880 Hz; same length, peak ~0.23.
The imposed buzz glisses up a decade across the file while the clean quiet material is untouched.

known_issues: gate's breakpoint path is broken (same machinery as submode 1's clip_level: value-invariant near-silent output); keep gate scalar. depth and freq breakpoints are healthy.
gate 0 renders digital silence; deterministic; unipolar material accepted; stereo refused 'Application doesn't work with this type of infile.' -> mono.
Duration static and sample-exact on tones, flat noise and unipolar clicks (88200 frames each).
